prompt:
Create a stdlib-only Python package `ledger/` that reads a plain-text money ledger and prints summaries, with unittest tests in tests/ (run with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`). The parts share one data type, so keep to these interfaces exactly.
1. ledger/model.py: a frozen dataclass `Entry(date: datetime.date, description: str, amount: decimal.Decimal, category: str)`.
2. ledger/parse.py: `parse(text: str) -> list[Entry]`. One entry per line: `YYYY-MM-DD | description | amount | category` (fields separated by `|`, surrounding spaces stripped). Blank lines and lines whose first non-space character is `#` are skipped. `amount` is a decimal with an optional leading `-` and at most 2 decimal places (`12`, `-3.5`, `1200.00`); `category` is stored lowercased; `description` must not be empty. Any malformed line raises `ValueError` whose message starts with `line N:` (N counts every line of the input from 1).
3. ledger/report.py: `balance(entries) -> Decimal` (sum of amounts); `by_category(entries) -> dict[str, Decimal]` (sum per category, keys in alphabetical order); `monthly(entries) -> dict[str, Decimal]` (net per `YYYY-MM`, keys in chronological order). Empty input gives `Decimal('0')` / `{}`.
4. ledger/cli.py with `main(argv: list[str]) -> int`, also runnable as `python3 -m ledger` (add ledger/__main__.py). `summary FILE` prints one `<category>: <amount>` line per category (alphabetical) then `total: <amount>`; `monthly FILE` prints one `<YYYY-MM>: <amount>` line per month (chronological). Amounts always print with exactly 2 decimals (`-3.50`, `0.00`). It returns 0 on success; on a missing file, a parse error or a bad command it prints `error: <message>` to stderr and returns 1 (for a parse error the message includes the `line N:` text).
Export Entry, parse, balance, by_category and monthly from ledger/__init__.py.
